prerequisites: Basic knowledge and competencies from degree programs or equivalent, including basic Physics and Mathematics.
Notions of Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer.
Basic computer skills for calculations and representation of results (e.g., Microsoft Excel or Matlab).
Basic knowledge of software for solving mass and energy balances (e.g., Engineering Equation Solver).

learning_outcomes.text: Correctly assess the energy efficiency of installations and their elements.
Rigorously execute thermodynamic and economic analyses of energy plants and installations.
Identify and quantify the most unfavorable aspects in the evaluation of processes and products in cogeneration plants.
Apply a systematic methodology for the thermoeconomic analysis of complex installations.

syllabus_topics: Feasibility of thermal processes and installations
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.4 x PA) + (0.6 x P1); otherwise, it is P1. P1 requires a minimum of 3.5 out of 10. For the extraordinary call, if minimums are met, the final grade is (0.15 x PA) + (0.15 x P1) + (0.7 x TE); otherwise, it is TE. TE requires a minimum of 3.5 out of 10. For differentiated assessment, if minimums are met, the final grade is (0.3 x P1) + (0.7 x TE); otherwise, it is TE. TE requires a minimum of 3.5 out of 10 for this modality.
